, m. (= Pali khaṇa), birth under favorable conditions. There are 8 akṣaṇa (q.v.) but only 1 kṣaṇa, viz., birth as a man in the ‘middle region’, where a Buddha is to be expected, at a time when he is born, and with the mental capacity to assimilate his doctrine (Pali): kṣaṇaṃ (acc.) ekaṃ buddhotpādaṃ suśobhanam; (bhavantu aṣṭākṣaṇavītivṛttāḥ, so read) āsādayantu kṣaṇarājam (the supreme favorable birth) uttamaṃ, (labhantu buddhehi samāgamaṃ sadā);; kṣaṇasampad, the good luck of (this) favorable birth; kṣaṇa-gati-pratilabdhena having obtained the lot of …; sarvakṣaṇopapannāḥ sattvā(ḥ), all creatures born under (the described) favorable conditions, cf. kṣaṇopapatti.(In kṣaṇāṃś ca, but keep kṣaṇāc ca with mss., and instantly.) Once, however, kṣaṇa in this sense seems to be [Page198-b] pluralized: so akṣaṇāni parivarjayitvā, kṣaṇā ca tasya bhavanti viśiṣṭā (but mss. bhavati viśiṣṭo, taking kṣaṇā as n. sg.,); the same vs even makes 8 kṣaṇa, obviously as mechanical pendant to the 8 akṣaṇa; so akṣaṇaṃ vai vijahāti sarvaṃ, aṣṭakṣaṇāś cāsya viśiṣṭa bhonti. This is a secondary distortion. In dullabho 'dya labhitaḥ kṣaṇavaro amṛto, today has been obtained the immortal (nectar-like?) excellent favorable birth that is hard to obtain, followed by 13 … varjitā (a)kṣaṇaduḥkhā asurasurapure, avoided the pains of unfavorable births in the cities of asuras and gods; evidently both kṣaṇa and akṣaṇa (the latter includes birth as a god!) are used in their standard meanings; but here the use of kṣaṇa is not strictly logical, since the Bodhisattva himself is speaking! [In; read kṣūṇa, q.v.]

, f., acc. to, = Skt. kṣaṇa, of a definite unit of time; but in line 3 the word is nt., kṣaṇāny; and in the parallel it seems to have been recorded first as m., kṣaṇaḥ (mss. however are corrupt), then nt., as in. See the passages, s.v. tatkṣaṇa. Prob. the fem. kṣaṇā is a mere corruption.]

, adj., empty (of the hands): read in kṣaṇikena (˚tena with 1 ms., v.l. kṣamikena) hastena gṛhaṃ gacchati, hato bhavati, went home empty-handed and was depressed (of a fowler who caught no birds);, read svakaṃ ca hastaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ (so 1 ms., v.l. kṣeṇikaṃ; em. implausibly) paśyati (having given away a beautiful lotus, and now regretting the gift); repeated. Is this an extension of the mg. of JM. khaṇika, idle, unemployed, out of work (which is itself derived from Skt. kṣaṇin, at leisure)? In any case the two passages confirm each other; kṣaṇika is certainly the true form in both, and the mg. is certain.

, adv. (? perh. for ˚ṇāc = ˚ṇāt, before c-) moment by moment, from moment to moment: (prose) kāścid (daughters of Māra) avaguṇṭhikayā (? see this) vadanāni chādayanti sma, kṣaṇe-kṣaṇā copadarśayanti sma. So with best mss., supported by ʼs ms. 1; Calc. with some mss. kṣaṇena.

(nt.; = Pali khamana, with dental n; not in Skt., tho normal formation from kṣam with -ana), tolerance, patience: paraṃ kṣamaṇam anāghātaśīlaṃ [Page199-a] ca saṃbhāvayet; a-kṣa˚, intolerance, akṣamaṇa-śīlatayā; in seems = kṣānti, q.v., prob. in sense of intellectual receptivity, vikalpasyāpravṛtti-kṣamaṇa-tā grāhyagrāhakaparijñayā sā kṣāntipāramitā.

, adj. or subst. nt. (= Pali khamanīya,, also with yāpanīya), tolerable, endurable (condition):, see s.v. yāpanīya. Both this form and kṣemaṇīya(-tara, q.v.) are used in what is clearly the same locution, bracketed with yāpanīya; kṣam˚ is supported by Pali khamanīya, but kṣemaṇīya-pṛccha, q.v., supports kṣem˚. Etymologically both forms can be justified in a way, but kṣemaṇīya looks strange as a derivative of kṣema (premaṇīya is not a perfect parallel) and may be a blend of kṣamaṇīya with kṣema. Or is it a direct imitation of premaṇīya, a near-synonym?

(m.? = Pali khara, said by to mean a saw, twice in vss.; used for cutting ivory or an elephantʼs tusk), a sharp cutting tool, perhaps a saw: (vs) kṣareṇa jihvām atha kartayāmi (cf., in prec. line, chinnāmi(!) nāsām krakacena vāsyāḥ; [Page199-b] krakaca, saw, in its Pali form kakaca, is the ʼs def. of khara).

, f. (= Pali khanti, used in this sense but not properly defined in Dictt., see, et alibi, see Index; good statement, cf. text and comm.;, et alibi), intellectual receptivity; the being ready in advance to accept knowledge; a preliminary stage leading to jñāna but distinguished from jñāna by the fact that it is still characterized by doubt,; the 8 kṣānti there referred to are paired with 8 corresponding jñāna to make up the 16 citta-kṣaṇāḥ, = caturāryasatyeṣu ṣoḍaśa kṣānti-jñānalakṣaṇāḥ; in this list are 8 pairs of jñānakṣānt and jñāna, e.g., first, duḥkhe dharma-jñānakṣānti, receptivity to knowledge of the truth in respect to misery, then duḥkhe dharmajñāna, du˚ 'nvayajñānakṣānti, du˚ 'nvayajñāna; and so with samudaye, nirodhe, and mārge instead of duḥkhe. So anutpattika-dharmakṣānti, q.v., receptivity to the fact that states-of-being have no origination; dharmanidhyāna-kṣānti, receptivity to reflection on the states of being, comm., see transl.; similarly, sarvadharmasvabhāvanidhyānakṣāntiḥ; dharmanidhyānādhimukti-kṣāntiḥ; samyaksaṃtīraṇā-kṣāntiḥ; avaivartikakṣānti-pratilabdhāś ca bhaviṣyanti, and will become possessed of the intellectual receptivity of non-returners (see avaivartika); ānulomikī kṣāntiḥ;; ānulomika-dharma-kṣānti-dharmālokamukham; nāhaṃ … teṣāṃ … ānulomikām api kṣāntiṃ vadāmi, kutaḥ punar buddhajñānam, I do not attribute to them even the intellectual receptivity that conforms (to continued religious development), still less Buddha-knowledge!; ghoṣānugā kṣānti, see ghoṣānuga; this with ānulomikī (or equivalent) and anutpattikadharma- (or equivalent) form a triad of kṣānti,; (see, cited s.v. ghoṣānuga); anutpāda- (and ˚de) kṣāntiḥ, q.v., and anupalambhadharma-kṣ˚, both = anutpattikadharma-kṣ˚; a different triad of kṣānti, (dharmanidhyāna-, duḥkhādhivāsanā-, paropakāradha(r)ma-); kṣānti is the 3d of the nirvedha-bhaga, q.v., (, comm.).

, ifc. Bhvr. (= kṣānti, q.v.; cf. Pali khantika), characterized by intellectual receptivity: gambhīra-kṣ˚; apratilabdha-kṣ˚; mṛdu-kṣāntikenāpi jñānena; pratilambha-kṣ˚ (pratilambha, acceptance, sc. of truth; not patience under censure,,).

, (1) spends, passes (time, with acc. kālam or some expression of time), is found in Skt. (), and the simple kṣipati is commoner in that sense (ibidem). It is strange that,, on khepeti (s.v. khipati), and others have overlooked that fact, regarded the usage as specifically Pali-BHS, and assumed confusion with kṣi, destroy. I have, to be sure, found no record of kṣepayati used absolutely in this sense in Skt., as it is in (vs) brahmaśakrabhavane nityaṃ sukhaṃ kṣepituṃ, to spend (time) happily forever in the home of Brahman and Śakra (2) exhausts, brings to an end, obliterates; here influence of kṣi, destroy, might more reasonably be suspected, yet Skt. kṣip is sometimes used in nearly or quite the same sense, s.v. kṣip 7 (; but as suspected, Calc. should be read kṣīyeran, not kṣiperan, see Crit. ed.); it prob. is an extension of the meaning spend (time). So (narakavedanīyāni karmāṇi) kṣepayitvā, having spent (exhausted) their deeds that had to be suffered-for in hells, which may illustrate the transition from spend (time) to exhaust; the change is complete in (vs) saptarātra bhaṇamānu … sā viyūha na pi śakya kṣepituṃ, tho described for a week, this splendor could not be exhausted (‘spent’). But it is doubtful whether any of these uses are strictly non-Skt.

, adj. (see below for Pali),, entangled in (or like; a maze or tangle of) cords (threads). Corresp. to guḍā-guñjika-bhūta, q.v., = Tib. dru gu (ball or skein of thread) ḥdziṅs pa (implicatus, embrouillé,) lta bu, become as it were mixed up in a skein of thread. Parts of this old cliché in and in l. c., and repeatedly in Pali, see s.v. guḷā, which misinterprets; an approximation to the Tib. transl. of this word (with jāta for bhuta) is given in Pali comms., e.g. : aho vatāhaṃ … lokasya tantrākulajātasya (q.v.; so mss.) guṇāvaguṇṭhitabhūtasyā- (here adds muñja-balbajajāta, q.v., with Pali) -javaṃjavasamāpannasyāsamāt etc. (for the rest see s.v. ājavaṃjava; Pali lacks this part, at least in most occurrences). The tradition, both Pali and BHS, is confused on the form of this word, but there seems no doubt of the essential meaning, as stated above. Instead of guṇa, thread, has guḍā, ball (sc. of thread; both Tib. dru gu and Pali comms. prove this mg., against). In Pali the mss. in different occurrences show guḷā, guḷi, guṇa, kulā, [Page213-a] kula, etc.; I suspect the orig. may have been guḍā (Pali guḷā), as in, but note the Pali v.l. guṇa as in; the mg. of the two is practically identical here. The second member appears in Pali as guṇṭhita, guṇṭhika, guṇḍika, guṇika, gaṇṭhita, gandhika, etc.; in avaguṇṭhita, in guñjika which seems to be unparalleled and uninterpretable. The orig. was most likely guṇṭhita; but possibly guṇṭhika (Pali, prob. based on a MIndic guṇṭhiya, really = guṇṭhita), or guṇḍita (AMg. guṇḍia, ˚ya).

The function of the gṛhapati-ratna is to discern the location of hidden treasures by means of the divya-cakṣus which he possesses, and bring those of them which are ownerless (asvāmika) into the possession of the king:; substantially the same statement in Pali, For this reason, no doubt, s.v. ratna translates gahapati by treasurer; but there is no clear evidence that he had precisely the functions which we should associate with that title. In Pali a gahapati (see s.v.) is, to be sure, often associated with seṭṭhi = śreṣṭhin; the Pali word is often rendered treasurer, but perhaps capitalist would be better (orig. guild-leader).

, m., (1) as in Skt., scope, range: svacitta-dṛśya-gocara-parijñāna-, knowledge of what has as its scope things perceptible to their own minds (, … the objective world as the manifestation of their own Mind, which is not what the words say); pratyātma-gatigocaram, what has as its scope the course of the individual self,;;; atra gambhīre buddhagocare, in regard to this profound sphere (range, scope) of the Buddha(s); similarly tathāgatagocarābhirataḥ; dhyāna-gocarāṇāṃ … laukikasamādhīnāṃ; etc., common, but hardly transcending Skt. limits; (2) (also quite close to Skt. usage, but closer to Pali locutions), association, the range of persons with whom one associates; in comp. or parallel with ācāra, right conduct; so also in Pali, ācāra-gocara-(dvandva! as all comms. agree; wrongly)-saṃpanna, perfect in conduct and personal associations, fully explained, where proper gocara is defined as avoiding the company of immoral persons, kings and courtiers, heretics, and impious families; so in a Bodhisattva must be ācāragocara-pratiṣṭhita, fixed in (right) conduct and associations, which, as the following makes clear, means (besides good conduct, ācāra) avoidance of kings and courtiers, heretics, worldlings, or even followers of the Hīnayāna (, in response to katamaś ca … bodhisattvasya … gocaraḥ); in this sense, saṃtoṣaṇīyā me sabrahmacāriṇo, yad uta tena tenācāra-gocara-samudācāreṇeti nihatamāno bhavati (does samudācāra, as third member of the cpd., mean address, manner of speaking to people?); prob. also saṃgaṇikayāpi vivekagocaraḥ, even with company, he is in association with solitude, i.e. he is not contaminated or distracted by crowds; (3) (= Pali id.) sustenance, provisions, food; particularly used (as in Pali) of food for monks: supriyā śrāvastīm abhisamprasthitā [Page215-b] gocaravyavalokanārthaṃ; (pātracīvaram ādāya) śrāvastīṃ gocarāya prasthitaḥ; gocara-grāma (= Pali ˚gāma), sustenance-village, a village where food is supplied to monks,;;;;; (read ˚grāmaṃ with ms. (in Skt. only nt., and not in these mgs.; also fail to record these mgs. except in cpd. gotrabhū, q.v.; but Pali gotta seems clearly used in mg. 1, below, in, in definition of gotrabhū: tam parittagottābhibhavanato mahaggatagottabhāvanato ca gotrabhū ti pi vuccati; note how Pali here associates the Sktized gotra-bhū with the MIndic gotta! contrast on), (1) lit. family, but in special technical sense of religious group or communion: pañcagotrāḥ, listed śrāvaka-yānābhisamayagotraḥ, pratyekabuddha-yānā˚, tathāgata-yānā˚, aniyatagotraḥ, a-gotraḥ; same five, with -gotraṃ, nt., (pañcābhisamaya-gotrāṇi); for the fourth, aniyataikatara-gotram,; in the sequel explains at length the first three; aniyata-, le gotra qui nʼest pas définitif,, is briefly treated in, aniyata-gotrakaḥ punar … triṣv apy eteṣu deśyamāneṣu yatrānunīyate tatrānuyojyaḥ syāt; apparently this is the class of people who may be drawn to whichever of the three yānas happens to be presented. The a-gotra is not explained but evidently means people outside of any Buddhist communion; in this sense understand gotrāgotraṃ kathaṃ, (religious) family and lack of it (dvandva cpd.). Only the first three gotras are listed; similarly contrasts śrāvaka-pratyekabuddha-gotrāṃ (acc. pl.) with tathāgata-gotrān. In; āryāṇāṃ gotraṃ is described as a state in which all normal conditions and activities are at an end, and in (continuation of the same) it is said, anulomaṃ tad gotraṃ nirvāṇasya. The relation of this to the three or five gotras is not quite clear. In the question, kena pravartitā gotrāḥ suvarṇamaṇimuktajāḥ, gotra is prob. used in this same sense, but the adj., sprung from gold, gems, and pearls, is obscure in application; one is tempted to see an allusion (metaphorically) to the next mg., cf. especially suvarṇagotra-vat and suratna-gotra-vat 10, with; but producing gold etc., which one would expect, seems philologically impossible; (2) mine, of gems or ores:, above; sarvaratnasaṃbhavotpattigotrākaramūlyajñāneṣu; dhātu-gotrāṇi, mines of ores (metals), ˚ṇi yaṃ paktvā suvarṇa-rūpya-vaiḍūryāṇy (˚vaid˚) abhinivartante, and (˚ūrya-sphaṭikāny˚); catvāro dhātu-gotrāḥ pradarśitāḥ; (3) like Skt. ākara, also origin: nikāyagati-gotrā ye, paraphrasing nikāyagati saṃbhavāt (labhyante); basis, source, cause, {{seea->seed||20210831||https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/80|}} punar etad gotram ādhāra ity ucyate, upastambho hetur niśraya upaniṣat pūrvaṃgamo nilaya ity ucyate … ( gotraṃ dvividhaṃ, prakṛtisthaṃ samudānītaṃ ca, natural and acquired …); tat punar gotraṃ bījam ity apy ucyate, dhātuḥ prakṛtir ity api (cf. gotra = bīja, hetu,); (4) prob. as special development of prec., kind, class, category (like Skt. jāti, of similar origin and lit. mg.): nānāratna-gotra-puṣpapratimaṇḍite, adorned with flowers (made of) various kinds of jewels; so prob. vijñapti-gotra-saṃchannam, covered by (various) classes of relative (worldly, practical) knowledge (see vijñapti).

, nt., confused with gahana, thicket, entanglement (?): in (prose) -durga-saṃsāra-kāntāragrahaṇa-dāruṇāto mahā-prapātāto uddharitvā, thinks that grahaṇa is a copyistʼs hyper-Skt. alteration of gahana, which is a near-synonym of kāntāra (esp. in Pali, where diṭṭhi-kantāra and diṭṭhi-gahana are often closely associated); in spite of this, I think grahaṇa may be sound and orig.: rescuing from a great abyss that is dreadful because of the grip of the forest of the saṃsāra etc. In occur four lines of verse in which the mss. repeatedly vary between gahana and grahaṇa; the text is both very corrupt and fragmentary; is a very earnest effort to disentangle it, but I find it hardly convincing, tho I am inclined to agree that puns are here contained, involving gahana, entanglement, obstruction, difficulty, as well as thicket, and grahaṇa, seizure, imprisonment (perhaps also eclipse, as by Rāhu, so Skt.); the text, with the most important vv.ll., reads: 14 vanagahanaṃ (mss. ˚grahanaṃ or ˚ṇaṃ) balagahanaṃ (3 mss. ˚grah˚) girigahanāni (em.; 5 mss. ˚gahanaṃ, one ˚grahaṇaṃ) tyāgagrahaṇāni (3 mss. ˚gahanāni), 15 viṣamāprati- (mss. viṣamapati-)-saṃniṣaṇṇavanāni tu manuṣyagahanāni (5 mss. ˚graha˚), 16 tṛṇagulmakaṇṭakalatākulāni vṛkṣagrahaṇā- (mss. ˚grahaṇya- or ˚nya-)gahanāni (3 mss. grahaṇāni), 17 śaṭhanikṛtipaiśunyāni tu manuṣyagahanāni (5 mss. ˚grahanāni or ˚ṇāni). Tho ʼs interpretation seems very dubious, I cannot suggest with confidence any improvements. The meter is meant for āryā. See also gahana, gahana-tā.
